name: turboexpander_parameter_identification
title: Turbo-expander parameter identification from new data (exercise)
summary: Steady model of a turbo-expander: an ideal isentropic nozzle followed by a Laval wheel. The equivalent throat area and the wheel diameter are the parameters identified from the additional expander data. The model then computes the shaft power.

origin.course: ULiège MSTh, repetition R4, exercise 2 continued

verification.summary: Compared with the stored solution of MSTh-SB-R4-Ex2-2.EES. compare_solution.py: 30 common variables, 8 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 0; only in CoolSolve: 1. Maximum relative difference 2.80e-01 on s_su (Air entropy reference, CoolSolve - EES = -1814 J/kg-K). A_thr and d_laval match. Shaft power 4370935 W versus 4378606 W.
verification.reference: EES stored solution in MSTh-SB-R4-Ex2-2.EES (EES X7.458)
verification.notes: 30 common variables. The tool prints 2.80e-01 on s_su; the exact ratio is 0.2801749. The extra CoolSolve name is PI, the built-in in U = PI*d_laval*N, not an unknown. The eight variables above rtol 0.001 are s_su, h_ex_n_s, h_thr, h_su, M_dot, W_dot, W_dot_in and v_thr. CoolSolve - EES on enthalpy is +126552.65, +126759.00 and +126341.19 J/kg. On entropy it is -1813.791 J/kg-K. A_thr and d_laval match. P_thr rel 2.41e-04 and eta_laval rel 7.86e-05, both under rtol 0.001. 14 iterations with .initials. Without .initials the size-5 block is SingularJacobian (analysis report: 18 total iterations, one Newton step, residual 899999). Negated velocity guesses return the positive root in 17 iterations. No --ees-units: stored values are already in Pa and J. The W_dot unit string is '-'.
